name: Raymond Castellano
presenting_complaint: Increasing breathlessness, drowsy, productive cough with green sputum

conditions: Severe COPD (known CO2 retainer, home oxygen)
medications: Home oxygen 1 L/min via nasal prongs
medical_history.social: Lives alone, ex-smoker (quit 3 years ago). Limited exercise tolerance (housebound). No documented advance care directive on file yet.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 71-year-old man with severe COPD and known CO2 retention presents with 3 days of worsening breathlessness, fever and green sputum. In the ambulance he was placed on high-flow oxygen 15 L/min via non-rebreather and is now drowsy and confused. Obs: RR 26, HR 104, SpO2 84%, Temp 38.1, GCS 13. He is flushed with a bounding pulse and a flapping tremor. ABG: pH 7.24, PaCO2 82 mmHg, PaO2 68 mmHg, HCO3 34.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: History of presenting complaint: 3 days of worsening dyspnoea, increased sputum volume and purulence (green), fever — infective exacerbation
Known severe COPD with documented CO2 retention, home oxygen use and previous NIV admission
Screen for the drowsiness/confusion as CO2 narcosis, and review pre-hospital oxygen (15 L/min non-rebreather) as the likely precipitant
Red-flag/DDx screen: chest pain (PE, pneumothorax), haemoptysis, orthopnoea/oedema (cardiac failure)
Ask about advance care directive / goals-of-care / documented ceiling of care early, as it changes the plan
objective: Urgent ABG (arterial blood gas) for pH and PaCO2 — do NOT rely on SpO2 alone
Titrate down inspired oxygen immediately: aim SpO2 88-92% via Venturi mask (e.g. 28%), reassess with repeat ABG
Respiratory exam: air entry, wheeze, crackles, signs of consolidation; look for asterixis, flushing, bounding pulse (hypercapnia)
Portable CXR (pneumonia/pneumothorax), ECG, FBC, UEC, CRP, blood cultures if febrile, sputum culture
Continuous cardiac and SpO2 monitoring; assess conscious state (GCS) and work of breathing serially
assessment: Infective exacerbation of COPD with type 2 respiratory failure and acute (decompensated) respiratory acidosis (pH 7.24, PaCO2 82)
CO2 narcosis precipitated by uncontrolled high-flow oxygen — reversible with controlled O2
Consider differentials/complications: pneumonia, PE, pneumothorax, cor pulmonale decompensation, cardiac failure
plan: Controlled oxygen therapy targeting SpO2 88-92% via Venturi mask (FIRST action) — wean the pre-hospital high-flow oxygen immediately and repeat ABG
Nebulised salbutamol 5 mg and ipratropium bromide 500 microgram — driven by AIR (not oxygen) in a known retainer, or with controlled O2 limitation
Systemic corticosteroid: prednisolone 50 mg orally OR hydrocortisone 100 mg IV
Antibiotics for infective exacerbation per local guideline (e.g. amoxicillin/doxycycline; broaden if pneumonia on CXR)
Commence NIV (BiPAP) for persistent respiratory acidosis (pH <7.35 with high PaCO2 despite controlled O2 and bronchodilators)
Escalate: call ED consultant and ICU; obtain serial ABGs; clarify ceiling of care / advance care directive before deciding on intubation
IV access, cardiac monitor, treat fever/sepsis, admit under medical/respiratory team with HDU/ICU review

critical_errors: Applying or continuing high-flow uncontrolled oxygen (e.g. 15 L/min non-rebreather) in a known CO2 retainer — worsening CO2 narcosis and respiratory arrest
Relying on SpO2 alone and failing to obtain an ABG to detect the respiratory acidosis/hypercapnia
Failing to commence NIV (BiPAP) for persistent respiratory acidosis despite optimal medical therapy
Over-correcting oxygen to a target that abolishes hypoxic drive instead of titrating to SpO2 88-92%
must_not_miss: Type 2 respiratory failure with acute respiratory acidosis requiring NIV (BiPAP)
CO2 narcosis from uncontrolled oxygen recognised and reversed with controlled O2 (target 88-92%)
ABG obtained early — diagnosis cannot be made on saturations alone
Advance care directive / ceiling of care clarified before escalation to intubation
